Here's how to reset your password for most online accounts:

1. Go to the login page of the website or app and click 'Forgot Password' or 'Reset Password'.
2. Enter the email address or username associated with your account.
3. Check your email inbox (and spam folder) for a password reset link. Click it within the time limit, usually 15-60 minutes.
4. Choose a new password. Use at least 12 characters with a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols.
5. Don't reuse passwords across different sites. Use a password manager like Bitwarden, 1Password, or Apple's Keychain to generate and store unique passwords.
6. If you have two-factor authentication enabled, you may need to verify your identity with a code sent to your phone or authenticator app.
7. After resetting, log in with your new password. Update any saved passwords in your browser if prompted.

If you don't receive the reset email, check your spam folder, verify you're using the correct email address, or contact the site's support team. Some sites also offer SMS-based password reset.

Here's how to connect to WiFi:

On Windows: Click the WiFi icon in the system tray (bottom right). Select your network from the list, click Connect, and enter the password.

On Mac: Click the WiFi icon in the menu bar (top right). Select your network and enter the password.

On iPhone/iPad: Open Settings, tap WiFi, select your network, and enter the password.

On Android: Open Settings, tap Network & Internet or Connections, tap WiFi, select your network, and enter the password.

If you can't find your network: make sure WiFi is turned on, move closer to the router, and refresh the network list. If the network still doesn't appear, try restarting your device and the router.

If you're connecting to a public or guest network: you may need to open a browser and accept terms or enter a code from the front desk.

The WiFi password is often printed on a sticker on the router itself. If you've forgotten your home WiFi password, you can find it in your device's WiFi settings or on the router admin page (usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1).

Here's how to take a screenshot on different devices:

On Windows: Press Windows + Shift + S to open the Snipping Tool and select an area. Or press Print Screen (PrtScn) to capture the whole screen, or Alt + Print Screen for just the active window.

On Mac: Press Command + Shift + 3 for the full screen. Command + Shift + 4 to select an area. Command + Shift + 5 for the screenshot toolbar with more options.

On iPhone/iPad (with Face ID): Press the side button and volume up button simultaneously. On models with Home button: press the Home and side/top button together.

On Android: Press the power button and volume down button simultaneously. On some Samsung phones, swipe the edge of your hand across the screen.

Screenshots are usually saved to your desktop or screenshots folder. On phones, they appear in your Photos or Gallery app.

Here's how to clear your browser cache:

On Chrome: Click the three dots (top right), go to More Tools > Clear Browsing Data. Select 'Cached images and files' and 'Cookies'. Choose a time range (All time for a complete refresh). Click Clear data.

On Firefox: Click the hamburger menu (top right), go to Settings > Privacy & Security. Under Cookies and Site Data, click Clear Data. Check both boxes and click Clear.

On Safari: Go to Safari > Clear History in the menu bar. Choose how far back to clear and click Clear History.

On Edge: Click the three dots (top right), go to Settings > Privacy, search, and services. Under Clear browsing data, click Choose what to clear. Select what you want to clear and click Clear now.

Clearing cache can fix issues like websites not loading correctly, showing outdated content, or login problems. You'll be signed out of most websites after clearing, so make sure you know your passwords.

Here's how to back up your phone:

iPhone: Go to Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > iCloud Backup. Tap 'Back Up Now'. Or connect to a computer, open Finder (or iTunes on older Windows), select your device, and click 'Back Up Now'. iCloud backups include device settings, app data, messages, and photos if you have iCloud Photos enabled.

Android: Go to Settings > Google > Backup. Make sure 'Back up by Google One' is turned on. This backs up app data, call history, contacts, and settings. For photos, open Google Photos and make sure backup is enabled.

Best practices: Keep automatic backup turned on. Make sure your phone is connected to WiFi when backing up to avoid using mobile data. Check that your backup completed successfully after major updates or before getting a new phone.

For photos specifically: consider using Google Photos (free unlimited storage at reduced quality), iCloud Photos, or Amazon Photos (free for Prime members).

Here's how to print a document:

1. Open the document, photo, or web page you want to print.
2. Press Ctrl+P (Windows) or Command+P (Mac) to open the print dialog.
3. Select your printer from the dropdown menu. If you don't see your printer, make sure it's turned on and connected to the same network.
4. Choose your settings:
   - Copies: how many copies you need
   - Pages: all pages, current page, or a range (like 1-5)
   - Color: color or black and white (black and white is cheaper)
   - Double-sided: print on both sides to save paper
   - Orientation: portrait (vertical) or landscape (horizontal)
5. Click Print. If nothing happens, check that the printer has paper and isn't showing an error.

Printer not working? Try these quick fixes: check for paper jams, make sure the ink or toner isn't empty, restart the printer, or run the printer's troubleshooting tool from your computer's settings.

Here's how to secure your home WiFi network:

1. Change the default admin password on your router. Default passwords like 'admin' are easily guessed. Log in to your router (usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1) and change it.
2. Use WPA2 or WPA3 encryption. Never use WEP or leave your network open. Find this in your router's wireless security settings.
3. Change your WiFi network name (SSID) to something that doesn't identify you or your address.
4. Disable WPS (WiFi Protected Setup) — it's a security vulnerability that makes it easier for attackers to guess your password.
5. Keep your router's firmware updated. Check for updates in the router admin panel or enable automatic updates if available.
6. Use a strong WiFi password: at least 12 characters with a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols.
7. Consider setting up a guest network for visitors so they don't have access to your main network's devices.
8. Disable remote management of your router unless you absolutely need it.
